passages.text: Of Solomon.
passages.sermon:
Solomon is the subject.
He is the son of David.
He is a king of Israel.
This psalm is about Solomon.

passages.text: Endow the king with Your justice, O God, and the son of the king with Your righteousness.
passages.sermon:
Solomon wrote this prayer.
He speaks to God.
He asks God to give justice to the king.
He asks God to give righteousness to the king’s son.
passages.original: לִשְׁלֹמֹ֨ה׀ אֱ‍ֽלֹהִ֗ים מִ֭שְׁפָּטֶיךָ לְמֶ֣לֶךְ תֵּ֑ן וְצִדְקָתְךָ֥ לְבֶן־ מֶֽלֶךְ׃

passages.text: May he judge Your people with righteousness and Your afflicted with justice.
passages.sermon:
Solomon is the king.
God gives Solomon authority.
Solomon judges God's people.
He uses righteousness to judge them.
Solomon judges the afflicted people.
He uses justice to judge the afflicted.
passages.original: יָדִ֣ין עַמְּךָ֣ בְצֶ֑דֶק וַעֲנִיֶּ֥יךָ בְמִשְׁפָּֽט׃

passages.text: May the mountains bring peace to the people, and the hills bring righteousness.
passages.sermon:
This passage speaks about the king Solomon.
Solomon is the son of David.
God gives Solomon wisdom and justice.
The mountains bring peace to the people.
The hills bring righteousness.
passages.original: יִשְׂא֤וּ הָרִ֓ים שָׁ֘ל֥וֹם לָעָ֑ם וּ֝גְבָע֗וֹת בִּצְדָקָֽה׃

passages.text: May he vindicate the afflicted among the people; may he save the children of the needy and crush the oppressor.
passages.sermon:
God is the judge.
God cares for the afflicted people.
God vindicates the afflicted among the people.
God saves the children of the needy.
God crushes the oppressor.
passages.original: יִשְׁפֹּ֤ט׀ עֲ‍ֽנִיֵּי־ עָ֗ם י֭וֹשִׁיעַ לִבְנֵ֣י אֶבְי֑וֹן וִֽידַכֵּ֣א עוֹשֵֽׁק׃

passages.text: May they fear him as long as the sun shines, as long as the moon remains, through all generations.
passages.sermon:
The people will fear him.
They will fear him as long as the sun shines.
They will fear him as long as the moon remains.
They will fear him through all generations.
passages.original: יִֽירָא֥וּךָ עִם־ שָׁ֑מֶשׁ וְלִפְנֵ֥י יָ֝רֵ֗חַ דּ֣וֹר דּוֹרִֽים׃

passages.text: May he be like rain that falls on freshly cut grass, like spring showers that water the earth.
passages.sermon:
This passage describes the ideal king.
The king brings blessing to his people.
He is gentle and life-giving.
He is like rain that falls on freshly cut grass.
He is like spring showers that water the earth.
passages.original: יֵ֭רֵד כְּמָטָ֣ר עַל־ גֵּ֑ז כִּ֝רְבִיבִ֗ים זַרְזִ֥יף אָֽרֶץ׃

passages.text: May the righteous flourish in his days and prosperity abound, until the moon is no more.
passages.sermon:
The righteous will flourish in his days.
Peace will be abundant.
This will last as long as the moon remains.
This blessing will continue for all time.
passages.original: יִֽפְרַח־ בְּיָמָ֥יו צַדִּ֑יק וְרֹ֥ב שָׁ֝ל֗וֹם עַד־ בְּלִ֥י יָרֵֽחַ׃

passages.text: May he rule from sea to sea, and from the Euphrates to the ends of the earth.
passages.sermon:
This passage describes a king who rules with great authority.
He rules from one sea to another sea.
He rules from the Euphrates River to the farthest parts of the earth.
His rule covers all lands.
passages.original: וְ֭יֵרְדְּ מִיָּ֣ם עַד־ יָ֑ם וּ֝מִנָּהָ֗ר עַד־ אַפְסֵי־ אָֽרֶץ׃

passages.text: May the nomads bow before him, and his enemies lick the dust.
passages.sermon: The king is righteous.\r\nNomads bow before him.\r\nHis enemies lick the dust.
passages.original: לְ֭פָנָיו יִכְרְע֣וּ צִיִּ֑ים וְ֝אֹיְבָ֗יו עָפָ֥ר יְלַחֵֽכוּ׃

passages.text: May the kings of Tarshish and distant shores bring tribute; may the kings of Sheba and Seba offer gifts.
passages.sermon:
The kings of Tarshish will bring tribute.
The kings from distant shores will also bring tribute.
The kings of Sheba will offer gifts.
The kings of Seba will also offer gifts.
passages.original: מַלְכֵ֬י תַרְשִׁ֣ישׁ וְ֭אִיִּים מִנְחָ֣ה יָשִׁ֑יבוּ מַלְכֵ֥י שְׁבָ֥א וּ֝סְבָ֗א אֶשְׁכָּ֥ר יַקְרִֽיבוּ׃

passages.text: May all kings bow down to him and all nations serve him.
passages.sermon: All kings will bow down to him.\r\nAll nations will serve him.
passages.original: וְיִשְׁתַּחֲווּ־ ל֥וֹ כָל־ מְלָכִ֑ים כָּל־ גּוֹיִ֥ם יַֽעַבְדֽוּהוּ׃

passages.text: For he will deliver the needy who cry out and the afflicted who have no helper.
passages.sermon:
God is the subject of this passage.
God acts with compassion and power.
God delivers needy people who cry out for help.
God helps afflicted people who have no one to help them.
passages.original: כִּֽי־ יַ֭צִּיל אֶבְי֣וֹן מְשַׁוֵּ֑עַ וְ֝עָנִ֗י וְֽאֵין־ עֹזֵ֥ר לֽוֹ׃

passages.text: He will take pity on the poor and needy and save the lives of the oppressed.
passages.sermon:
God cares for the poor.
God cares for the needy.
God saves the lives of the oppressed.
God rescues those who suffer.
passages.original: יָ֭חֹס עַל־ דַּ֣ל וְאֶבְי֑וֹן וְנַפְשׁ֖וֹת אֶבְיוֹנִ֣ים יוֹשִֽׁיעַ׃

passages.text: He will redeem them from oppression and violence, for their blood is precious in his sight.
passages.sermon:
God cares for the needy and the oppressed.
God sees their suffering.
God will rescue them from oppression.
God will save them from violence.
Their lives are valuable to God.
God considers their blood precious.
passages.original: מִתּ֣וֹךְ וּ֭מֵחָמָס יִגְאַ֣ל נַפְשָׁ֑ם וְיֵיקַ֖ר דָּמָ֣ם בְּעֵינָֽיו׃

passages.text: Long may he live! May gold from Sheba be given him. May people ever pray for him; may they bless him all day long.
passages.sermon:
This passage speaks about a king who cares for the poor and needy.
He saves the lives of the oppressed.
May this king live a long life.
May people bring him gold from Sheba.
May people always pray for him.
May people bless him all day long.
passages.original: וִיחִ֗י וְיִתֶּן־ לוֹ֮ מִזְּהַ֪ב שְׁ֫בָ֥א וְיִתְפַּלֵּ֣ל בַּעֲד֣וֹ תָמִ֑יד כָּל־ הַ֝יּ֗וֹם יְבָרֲכֶֽנְהֽוּ׃

passages.text: May there be an abundance of grain in the land; may it sway atop the hills. May its fruit trees flourish like the forests of Lebanon, and its people like the grass of the field.
passages.sermon:
God is the one who blesses the land.
May there be much grain in the land.
May the grain grow on the tops of the hills.
May the fruit of the land be like the forests of Lebanon.
May the people in the cities grow and spread like the grass of the earth.
passages.original: יְהִ֤י פִסַּת־ בַּ֨ר׀ בָּאָרֶץ֮ בְּרֹ֪אשׁ הָ֫רִ֥ים יִרְעַ֣שׁ כַּלְּבָנ֣וֹן פִּרְי֑וֹ וְיָצִ֥יצוּ מֵ֝עִ֗יר כְּעֵ֣שֶׂב הָאָֽרֶץ׃

passages.text: May his name endure forever; may his name continue as long as the sun shines. In him may all nations be blessed; may they call him blessed.
passages.sermon:
This passage speaks about a king who rules with justice and righteousness.
His name will last forever.
His name will continue as long as the sun shines.
All nations will find blessing in him.
All nations will call him blessed.
passages.original: יְהִ֤י שְׁמ֨וֹ לְֽעוֹלָ֗ם לִפְנֵי־ שֶׁמֶשׁ֮ יָנִין שְׁ֫מ֥וֹ וְיִתְבָּ֥רְכוּ ב֑וֹ כָּל־ גּוֹיִ֥ם יְאַשְּׁרֽוּהוּ׃

passages.text: Blessed be the LORD God, the God of Israel, who alone does marvelous deeds.
passages.sermon:
The LORD is God.
He is the God of Israel.
He alone does marvelous deeds.
Blessed be the LORD God.
passages.original: בָּר֤וּךְ׀ יְהוָ֣ה אֱ֭לֹהִים אֱלֹהֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֑ל עֹשֵׂ֖ה נִפְלָא֣וֹת לְבַדּֽוֹ׃

passages.text: And blessed be His glorious name forever; may all the earth be filled with His glory. Amen and amen.
passages.sermon:
God is the Lord.
God’s name is glorious.
God’s glorious name is blessed forever.
God’s glory fills all the earth.
Amen.
Amen.
passages.original: וּבָר֤וּךְ׀ שֵׁ֥ם כְּבוֹד֗וֹ לְע֫וֹלָ֥ם וְיִמָּלֵ֣א כְ֭בוֹדוֹ אֶת־ כֹּ֥ל הָאָ֗רֶץ אָ֘מֵ֥ן׀ וְאָמֵֽן׃

passages.text: Thus conclude the prayers of David son of Jesse.
passages.sermon:
David is the son of Jesse.
David prayed many prayers.
These are the prayers of David.
All the prayers of David end here.
passages.original: כָּלּ֥וּ תְפִלּ֑וֹת דָּ֝וִ֗ד בֶּן־ יִשָֽׁי׃
